mind_tricks.title: Don't Solve Every Puzzle: The 60-Second Scan
mind_tricks.title_hi: हर पहेली को तुरंत मत छेड़ें: 60-सेकंड स्कैन नियम
mind_tricks.when_to_use: First 60 seconds of any Prelims Reasoning section
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Exam setters intentionally place 1 difficult or uncertain puzzle early in the section to trap candidates in a 5-minute time sink. By quickly scanning and identifying the 3 easiest sets first, you secure 15 marks with maximum confidence.
mind_tricks.method: Spend the first 45-60 seconds browsing all 35 questions. Attempt all standalone speed questions first (Syllogism, Inequality, Alphanumeric, Coding) in 6-7 minutes (securing ~15 marks). Then attempt the 2 most straightforward puzzles (Floor/Flat or Month/Date with fixed base) before touching uncertain seating.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Saves 4-6 minutes and eliminates exam panic
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Blindly beginning with Question 1 even if it's a 3-variable uncertain linear puzzle.

mind_tricks.title: Start Puzzles with Fixed Anchor Clues Only
mind_tricks.title_hi: पहेलियाँ केवल निश्चित आधार (Anchor Clues) से शुरू करें
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Any Floor, Flat, Month, or Box puzzle
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Weak relative clues like 'A sits near B' create 4+ branching permutations. An anchor clue fixes an absolute coordinate (e.g. 'P sits on the lowermost floor' or 'Q attends seminar on 14th April') and immediately reduces branches to 1 or 2.
mind_tricks.method: Scan the text for keywords: 'extreme end', 'bottom-most / top floor', 'corner', 'adjacent to vacant', 'date with 31 days'. Plot this anchor first.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Reduces solving time from 4.5 minutes to 2 minutes
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Reading linearly sentence by sentence and trying to place relative conditions prematurely.

mind_tricks.title: Syllogism: 'Only a few' Instant Dual-Truth
mind_tricks.title_hi: न्याय निगमन: 'Only a few' का अचूक दोहरा नियम
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Whenever statement contains 'Only a few A are B'
mind_tricks.why_it_works: 'Only a few' is mathematically equivalent to TWO simultaneous conditions: (1) Some A are B [Positive], and (2) Some A are NOT B [Negative].
mind_tricks.method:
Rule 1: All A can NEVER be B. Any conclusion stating 'All A being B is a possibility' is AUTOMATICALLY FALSE.
Rule 2: But All B can be A! Unless restricted by another statement, 'All B being A is a possibility' is ALWAYS TRUE.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Answers conclusions in 5 seconds without drawing complex Venn diagrams
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Treating 'Only a few' as simple 'Some' and marking 'All A are B is a possibility' as true.

mind_tricks.title: Inequality: The Open Door / Gatekeeper Method
mind_tricks.when_to_use: All linear and semi-colon inequality questions
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Visualizes relational flow as traveling through doors. You can travel from the open wide mouth to the pointed vertex: A > B means door is open from A to B, closed from B to A.
mind_tricks.method:
To verify 'P > Q':
1. Check if path starts at P and moves towards Q with doors open.
2. Ensure at least one strict '>' door exists on the trail.
3. If at any point you meet opposite signs (e.g. > and <), path is blocked and relation is impossible.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Allows solving 5 inequality questions in under 45 seconds directly on screen
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Rewriting the statements on rough paper instead of tracing directly on screen.

mind_tricks.title: Blood Relations: Generation Integer Method
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Evaluating coded relations or determining relationship between two distant individuals
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Replaces confusing genealogical strings with simple arithmetic addition.
mind_tricks.method:
Grandparents = +2 | Parents/Uncle/Aunt = +1 | Siblings/Spouse = 0 | Children/Niece/Nephew = -1 | Grandchildren = -2.
If question asks 'How is A related to D', add the generational step integers between them. If the sum is +1, A MUST be from parent generation (father/mother/uncle/aunt). Immediately eliminate brother, son, grandfather options!
mind_tricks.time_saved: Instantly eliminates 3 out of 5 options without drawing tree
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Drawing large family trees for simple coded expressions.

mind_tricks.title: Direction: Cartesian Coordinate Shortcut (X, Y)
mind_tricks.title_hi: दिशा एवं दूरी: कार्तीय निर्देशांक विधि (East = +X, North = +Y)
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Person takes multiple turns and question asks final distance/direction from start
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Translates turning movements into independent orthogonal components on an (X, Y) plane.
mind_tricks.method:
East = +X, West = -X, North = +Y, South = -Y.
Sum all X coordinates: ΔX.
Sum all Y coordinates: ΔY.
Shortest distance = √(ΔX² + ΔY²).
Direction is derived directly from signs of (ΔX, ΔY). E.g. (+5, -3) = East-South = South-East!
mind_tricks.time_saved: Cuts drawing and measurement errors by 80%
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Drawing turns with wrong scale, making 10m look shorter than 5m and misjudging alignment.

mind_tricks.title: Coding: Opposites Sum to 27 & EJOTY Grid
mind_tricks.title_hi: कोडिंग: विपरीत अक्षरों का योग 27 एवं EJOTY सूत्र
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Letter manipulation, opposite letter pairs, new pattern coding
mind_tricks.why_it_works: The position of any letter from the front (1 to 26) and from the back (26 to 1) always sums to 27.
mind_tricks.method:
Remember anchors: E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25.
Opposite of any letter = 27 - position. E.g., Letter 'H' is 8th. Opposite = 27 - 8 = 19 (S). High-School (HS).
Memorable mnemonic pairs: AZ (Azad), BY (Boy), CX (Crux), DW (Dew), EV (Even), FU (Full), GT (GT Road), HS (High School), IR (Indian Railway), JQ (Jungle Queen), KP (Kurta Pyjama), LO (Love), MN (Man).
mind_tricks.time_saved: Recalls letter codes in under 1 second
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Writing the entire A-Z alphabet on rough sheet during precious exam minutes.

mind_tricks.title: Alphanumeric Series: Direction Addition & Subtraction
mind_tricks.title_hi: वर्ण-संख्या श्रृंखला: समान दिशा घटाएँ, विपरीत दिशा जोड़ें
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Questions like 'Which element is 6th to the left of 17th from left end?'
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Moving left from a left-referenced position moves you back towards the start; moving right from a left-referenced position moves you forward.
mind_tricks.method:
Same directions -> SUBTRACT (Left - Left or Right - Right)
Opposite directions -> ADD (Left + Right or Right + Left)
Example: '7th to the right of 19th from left end' = Opposite directions -> (19 + 7) = 26th from left end!
'5th to the right of 18th from right end' = Same directions -> (18 - 5) = 13th from right end!
mind_tricks.time_saved: Answers in 4 seconds with zero manual hopping on screen
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Counting 18 from right, and then physically counting 5 to the right one by one.

mind_tricks.title: Input-Output: The Step-Indexing Shortcut
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Arranging words and numbers without writing every intermediate step
mind_tricks.why_it_works: Elements shift according to predetermined sorting rank (e.g. smallest number left, alphabetical word right). If an element naturally sits in its final slot when prior elements move, it gets 'auto-arranged' without a new step.
mind_tricks.method: Identify the target sequence. Label each element with its required order (L1, L2, L3 on left; R1, R2, R3 on right). Track which elements get auto-placed. Total steps required = Total elements - Auto-arranged elements.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Solves a 5-mark Mains set in 2 minutes instead of 5 minutes
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Writing out all 6 steps line by line on paper.

mind_tricks.title: Critical Reasoning: The Negation Test for Assumptions
mind_tricks.title_hi: कथन एवं पूर्वधारणा: नकारात्मक परीक्षण (Negation Test)
mind_tricks.when_to_use: Confused between two plausible assumptions in Mains
mind_tricks.why_it_works: An assumption is the unstated foundation of the argument. If the foundation is destroyed (negated), the entire statement becomes pointless or absurd.
mind_tricks.method: Take the assumption option and temporarily add 'NOT' to it. Read the statement again. If the statement completely falls apart, then that assumption is 100% VALID. If the statement can still stand even if the assumption is false, the assumption is INVALID.
mind_tricks.time_saved: Guarantees 100% accuracy in high-stake Mains verbal reasoning
mind_tricks.common_mistake: Choosing options based on personal real-life opinion rather than logical necessity.

topper_vs_normal.problem: Statements: A > B ≥ C; C = D < E. Conclusion: A > D

normal_method.description: Writes down statement on rough paper: A > B ≥ C = D < E. Slowly checks if A is greater than B, B is greater than or equal to C, C equals D, and verifies each sign step-by-step.

topper_method.description: Scans directly on computer screen. Locates A and D. Notes path: A > B ≥ C = D. Gate is open throughout from A to D, and contains a strict '>' symbol. Immediately clicks 'True'.

topper_vs_normal.problem: Statements: Only a few Phones are Laptops. All Laptops are Tablets. Conclusion: All Phones being Laptops is a possibility.

normal_method.description: Draws 3 overlapping circles on rough paper. Tries to imagine whether the phone circle can expand into the laptop circle, checks if there is any violation, ponders for 45 seconds.

topper_method.description: Recalls rule: 'Only a few Phones are Laptops' means Some Phones are definitely NOT Laptops. Hence All Phones can never be Laptops. Possibility is instantly False without lifting pen.

topper_vs_normal.problem: In a row of 45 students, A is 16th from the left. What is A's rank from the right end?

normal_method.description: Draws a line with 45 tally marks or counts on fingers. Thinks 45 - 16 = 29, and marks 29.
normal_method.trap_note: Fails to add 1 and marks 29, getting negative marks!

topper_method.description: Applies mental formula: Rank from Right = Total - Rank from Left + 1 = 45 - 16 + 1 = 30. Solved in 5 seconds mentally.

topper_vs_normal.problem: Which element is 5th to the left of 18th from the left end in a 30-element sequence?

normal_method.description: Counts 18 elements from the left end on the monitor. Stops finger at 18th. Then counts 5 elements backwards to the left.

topper_method.description: Identifies same direction: Left and Left -> Subtract: 18 - 5 = 13th from left end. Directly counts to 13th element in one single pass.

flashcards.front: What does 'Only A are B' mean in standard logical terms?
flashcards.back: It means 'All B are A' AND 'B can have NO relationship with any other circle'. B is strictly exclusive to A.

flashcards.front: What are the valid Complementary Pairs for 'Either-Or'?
flashcards.back:
1. Some + No
2. Some + Some Not
(Note: 'All + No' is NOT an Either-Or pair; 'All + Some Not' only if subjects and predicates match order).

flashcards.front: What is the formula for Total persons in a row?
flashcards.back: Total = (Rank from Left / Top + Rank from Right / Bottom) - 1

flashcards.front: What is the sum of positions of any letter and its opposite letter?
What happens if opposite signs (e.g. > and <) appear between two elements in an inequality chain?
flashcards.back: No definite relationship can be determined. Any definite conclusion between them is FALSE. Only an Either-Or (with all 3 possibilities >, <, =) can hold.

flashcards.front: Where does the shadow of an object fall at Sunrise?
flashcards.back: At Sunrise (Sun in East), all shadows fall towards the WEST. At Sunset (Sun in West), shadows fall towards the EAST.
